source.title: Algorithmic Regularization in Learning Deep Homogeneous Models: Layers are Automatically Balanced
source.authors: S. Du; Wei Hu; J. Lee

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies layer balancing and matrix factorization convergence, not training classification error on benchmarks or the specific behaviors in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports layer-balance measurements for a three-layer ReLU network. It does not report classification error, so these results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study establishes norm-balance invariants and matrix-factorization convergence. It does not test any version's specified behavior: initialization comparisons measure layer norms, not learning speed, gradient propagation or trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion, but needs qualifications: gradient flow preserves initial squared-norm differences, so initially small differences remain small; it does not eliminate arbitrary initial imbalance. For general-rank asymmetric matrix factorization, sufficiently small random initialization and diminishing step sizes yield a limit with reconstruction error at most epsilon with high probability. For rank one, sufficiently small constant step sizes yield linear convergence with constant probability over initialization.
record.recipe_differences: The neural-network experiment uses gradient descent to measure layer balance with quadratic loss; it does not test benchmark classification error. The matrix-factorization analysis is theoretical and outside the claim versions’ benchmark setting.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported layer-balance outcome differs between balanced and unbalanced initialization conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: The three-layer ReLU experiment reports approximately preserved adjacent-layer squared-norm differences and ratios approaching 1 under small balanced or unbalanced initialization, subject to the numerical inconsistencies identified above.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-step gradient descent approximately preserves initial layer squared-norm differences in the tested homogeneous network; relative imbalance can shrink as norms grow.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 2.1–2.3 prove that gradient flow preserves squared-norm differences for homogeneous networks, including convolutional networks. Theorems 3.1–3.2 establish convergence guarantees for unregularized asymmetric matrix factorization under specified initialization and step sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Homogeneity induces balance invariants under gradient flow, and approximate balance can enable convergence guarantees for discrete gradient descent in asymmetric matrix factorization.

record.problems: The empirical neural-network result uses one architecture and one quadratic-loss dataset; exact norm-ratio values are only shown in figures. The paper does not measure classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and model-size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequency and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention by residual shortcuts, special initialization or Fixup.
Initialization effects on learning speed, signal and gradient propagation, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: References to Xavier/Kaiming initialization and a claimed optimization advantage of ReLU over sigmoid do not establish any listed version: the study supplies no corresponding speed or depth comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size, training duration, or regularization.
Spurious minima frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training error in plain versus residual networks, including normalization and Fixup comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed, vanishing or exploding signals, trainable depth, orthogonal weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Training dynamics at and above learning-rate stability limits, including loss, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization effects on accuracy speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

conditions.value: Balanced: W1 entries N(0, 10^-4/100); W2 entries N(0, 10^-4/10); W3 entries N(0, 10^-4).

rows.measure: Adjacent-layer squared Frobenius norm differences and ratios
rows.value: Differences bounded by 0.14; after 10,000 iterations, squared norms are 42.90, 43.76 and 43.68; ratios approach 1 (figure).
rows.note: Measures layer balance, which none of the listed versions names; the figure describes ratios as approaching 1 but gives no exact values.
rows.check: The extracted values match Section 4, but the source is internally inconsistent: final squared norms 42.90 and 43.76 differ by 0.86, exceeding its stated all-iteration bound of 0.14. Preserve this discrepancy rather than treating both as verified measurements. Layer balance cannot determine any listed version.

rows.measure: Adjacent-layer squared Frobenius norm differences and ratios
rows.value: Differences bounded by 9 and change very little; after 10,000 iterations, squared norms are 55.50, 45.65 and 45.46; ratios become close to 1 after about 1,000 iterations (figure).
rows.note: Measures layer balance, which none of the listed versions names; the figure provides no exact ratio values.
rows.check: The extracted values match Section 4, but final squared norms 55.50 and 45.65 differ by 9.85, exceeding its stated bound of 9. The final first-to-second ratio is about 1.216, so closeness to 1 is qualitative. Layer balance cannot determine any listed version.
